assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, via the magic-wavelength idea and its realization in strontium and other species, moved timekeeping to fractional uncertainties of order 1e-18. This is a textbook case of a new measurement capability that opens further science: relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants, searches for dark matter and a path to redefining the second. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all high.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early Sr lattice clocks; Jun Ye led the highest-precision realizations and many-body/spin-exchange clock physics. A two-laureate award is coherent, though other groups (e.g., Ludlow/Oates/NIST, Lemonde, Takamoto) could be raised in discussion. Hall and Hansch were already honored in 2005 for the comb.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups worldwide have reproduced and improved the clocks, and comparisons between clocks now underpin the redefinition roadmap. The interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Exact priority split between the magic-wavelength proposal and the first demonstrations is something I recall from memory and have not verified.
Whether the committee views this as sufficiently distinct from the earlier frequency-comb recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Matter-wave interferometry gives inertial, gravitational and constant-measurement sensitivities that rival or exceed classical instruments (gravimeters, gyroscopes, fine-structure constant, tests of the equivalence principle). The field is built on careful experimental demonstration and has produced deployed instruments, which fits my emphasis on what can actually be measured.
assessment.attribution: Bordé supplied early theory of atom interferometry and the Ramsey-Bordé geometry; Pritchard demonstrated early atom interferometers and later precision metrology; Kasevich made the light-pulse gravimeter/gyroscope precision instruments. Holger Müller is also credited and a four-person list exceeds the three-person limit, so someone has to be left out; Chu and others not in the supplied credit would complicate the picture. Credit allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with commercial gravimeters and repeated independent demonstrations, but record sensitivities and tests of fundamental physics are still moving. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Which three of four credited names best capture the decisive contributions; Müller's contribution is later and mostly precision measurements.
Overlap with the 1997 and 2018 laser-cooling and trapping prizes in the subfield.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides the architecture for dispersive readout, strong coupling and gate control of superconducting qubits, and is the working basis of most current superconducting quantum processors. The work is original (Blais/Wallraff/Schoelkopf proposal and demonstration), clean and has opened an entire field.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the Wallraff Nature 2004 demonstration form a natural trio, with Girvin not in the supplied names. The credit is fairly clear within the supplied names, though the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunneling in circuits overlaps the area.
assessment.maturity: Strong, independent confirmation across many labs and wide device adoption. The 2025 Nobel makes timing sensitive, but the cQED architecture itself is clearly mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wishes to honor a second superconducting-circuit prize so soon after 2025.
Girvin is a key theorist who is not in the supplied credit list, and I cannot verify how that affects fairness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coherent light-matter interfaces, including cavity QED with single atoms, quantum memories, and quantum-network nodes, form the physical basis for quantum repeaters and networks. This is close to my own field of quantum memories. I know how hard it is to reach high efficiency and long storage, and the field-defining demonstrations here are real, but it is a compound area.
assessment.attribution: Rempe (single-atom cavity QED and atom-photon state transfer), Kimble (quantum network vision and DLCZ-type architecture) and Lukin (EIT-based storage and photon-photon interactions) each have decisive work, but the topic spans several distinct achievements and different parts could be recognized separately. Others in quantum-memory work (Hau, Lvovsky, Gisin, Polzik) are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Rapid progress and many independent demonstrations, but practical quantum networks are still in early stages, so the maturity of the full compound topic is moderate.
uncertainties: The compound nature of the discovery may make it unfocused as a prize citation.
Quantum-memory performance continues to change and the field has not settled on a leading platform.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light injected into interferometers beats the standard quantum limit and is now operating in LIGO, Virgo and GEO600. This is a measurement-technique success: a quantum resource improving real instrument sensitivity. Caves's 1981 proposal is original, and the experimental squeezing record is clear.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the theoretical idea, Kimble made early squeezed-light experiments (with Slusher, Wu and collaborators not credited here), and Schnabel/GEO600 demonstrated the application. Mavalvala is also credited; the exact trio is not obvious. Slusher is notably missing and the experimental origin of squeezing in 1985 is not fully covered.
assessment.maturity: Operational in gravitational-wave detectors since 2019, giving strong confirmation and practical impact. Timely, although the 2017 prize covered LIGO.
uncertainties: Which experimentalists beyond the supplied names deserve credit for the first squeezing.
Possible view that this is an enabling technique of an already recognized discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 with ATLAS and CMS completed the Standard Model and rests on enormously demanding detector and analysis work. Scientific importance is beyond dispute, though the 2013 prize already honored the theory.
assessment.attribution: The prize rules limit to three people and the discovery was made by thousands; the proposed trio are the founding spokespersons and architects of the experiments, while Gianotti was spokesperson at the time of announcement. The allocation is unavoidably arbitrary and a committee may be reluctant to single out individuals from a collaboration of this size.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by two experiments and by subsequent properties measurements; timing is plausible but the attribution problem is severe.
uncertainties: Statute and tradition issues with large collaborations (the prize can go to organizations only in the Peace category).
Whether detector-leadership is viewed as a physics discovery contribution; I am working from memory about roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg-blockade tweezer arrays have delivered programmable quantum simulators and neutral-atom processors with hundreds of atoms, high-fidelity entangling gates and logical-qubit demonstrations. The experimental advances are striking and clearly measurement-rich AMO physics.
assessment.attribution: Saffman and Lukin proposed the blockade gate concept (with Jaksch, Cirac, Zoller et al. not credited here); Browaeys and Lukin built early experimental arrays (with Grangier, Regal, Ahn and others). Credit is crowded and unsettled, with the Jaksch-Cirac-Zoller blockade proposal an obvious absentee from this credited list.
assessment.maturity: Very recent growth and performance records are still being set; independent confirmation is strong but the field is still evolving and probably somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Credit for the original blockade proposal versus the later array experiments.
Future benchmarks for neutral-atom fault tolerance may change the picture.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube turned a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a neutrino telescope, with the 2013 discovery of a high-energy astrophysical flux, the TXS 0506+056 association in 2017 and the Galactic-plane detection in 2023. It is a new way of observing the universe, and the instrument itself is a major technical accomplishment.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the central figure for the concept and leadership; Karle and Spiering have important roles in construction and analysis, though this list leaves out other long-time leaders (e.g., Gaisser, Ahrens, Kowalski, Klein) and the AMANDA/Baikal predecessors. Credit is broad and partly collaborative.
assessment.maturity: Independently supported by KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD for related results; the source identification program is still young, but the diffuse flux is firmly established.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit and the lack of a clean three-person attribution.
Whether source identification is mature enough for a prize now.
